question: Should `memory.isolation` become a default-on security boundary for memory-core, and if so which `scope`, fallback, and path-encoding options are part of the supported runtime contract?
rationale: This PR changes privacy boundaries, stored memory layout, defaults, and user-facing config; automation can identify defects but cannot choose the product/security contract or acceptable upgrade behavior.

options.title: Default-on isolated memory
options.body: Require the PR to enforce isolation when the config block is absent, honor or remove every accepted option, document the upgrade path, and provide real builtin/QMD proof before merge.

options.title: Explicit opt-in first
options.body: Preserve current shared-memory behavior by default and make per-user isolation an opt-in mode until migrations and operator recovery are settled.

options.title: Defer to canonical design
options.body: Pause this PR and use the broader multi-user memory issue for a maintainer-owned design across memory backends and plugins.

recommendation.title: Default-on isolated memory
recommendation.body: Require the PR to enforce isolation when the config block is absent, honor or remove every accepted option, document the upgrade path, and provide real builtin/QMD proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of memory-core/SDK boundary refactors and storage-shape decisions around the touched files.
